prompt:
A SmartPark Media Operations management system that includes offline-first parking device event ingestion and a consumer-grade content experience for drivers and onsite staff. Regular Users sign in with a locally verified username and password to access a Vue.js web UI optimized for kiosk tablets and front-desk desktops, where they can search a library of audio announcements and short clips, save favorites, build and edit playlists, and share playlists internally via a copyable on-screen code that can be entered on another device (no external messaging). The UI provides a responsive search page with full-text queries, filters for tags, duration (for example, under 2 minutes), and recency (last 30 days), plus sorting by "Most Played," "Newest," and "Recommended." A "Now Playing" panel shows recent plays and session history, and explains recommendations using simple on-screen reasons such as "Based on your favorites: Safety, Overnight, Gate Issues." Administrators use an admin console to review asset uploads, manage blacklisted accounts, freeze accounts for a defined period (for example, 72 hours), and view operational dashboards for device status and content usage. Field Technicians access a device console view to validate that gate/camera/sensor events are being received, with clear feedback for duplicates, late arrivals, and buffered transmissions when connectivity between local nodes is intermittent.

The backend uses Laravel to expose REST-style APIs consumed by the Vue.js frontend over the local network, with MySQL as the system of record for users, roles, playlists, favorites, play history, search index tables, and device events. Parking device integration is implemented via reserved local interfaces (HTTP endpoints and optional file drop folders) for cameras, gates, and geomagnetic sensors; each event must include a device identifier, event type, and a unique idempotency key, and the server deduplicates within a 7-day window while also correcting out-of-order sequences using per-device monotonic counters and allowing controlled replay with audit trails. If the device gateway is offline, it buffers up to 10,000 events locally and retransmits using exponential backoff; the server accepts replays without double-applying side effects. The media resource center stores files on local disk with reference tracking so deleting an asset that is used by any playlist is blocked until replaced; uploads enforce format allowlists (JPEG/PNG/PDF/MP3/MP4), a 25 MB limit for images/docs and 250 MB for video, and basic fingerprint validation plus MIME sniffing to prevent disguised executables, with reserved hooks for future on-prem scanning tools without requiring internet. Performance and stability requirements include generating local thumbnails and multi-size crops (for example, 160/480/960 px widths), asynchronous indexing and recommendation candidate generation via Laravel queues, and automatic degradation that disables "Recommended" ranking and falls back to "Most Played" if API p95 latency exceeds 800 ms for 5 minutes or recommendation hit rate drops below 10%. Security requires salted password hashing, at-rest encryption for sensitive fields (for example, email if stored for profile only), masking in logs, soft-delete with a 30-day purge job for account deletion, and a local monitoring page that surfaces API error rate, queue backlog, and device ingestion health without any third-party telemetry.
